key_insight: Weak sinusoidal forcing can strongly reshape turbulence and particle clustering in a planar jet even when the mean flow stays nearly unchanged.
engineering_relevance: Low-frequency modulation offers a practical control knob for tuning particle dispersion and preferential concentration in jet-based mixing, spray, and process-flow systems.
method: Hot-wire anemometry measured carrier-flow turbulence at two Reynolds numbers.
High-speed particle imaging and Voronoi tessellations quantified dilute inertial-particle clustering.
Forced and unforced jets were compared over the forcing cycle to track phase-dependent turbulence and Stokes-number changes.
evidence_signal: Experiments at nozzle-height Reynolds numbers of about 4950 and 9900 showed up to 40% reduction in integral scale and 21–49% cycle-mean variations in clustering, with clustering peaking when Kolmogorov time scale was largest.
watch_item: The forcing is weak and far below the jet instability frequency, so the results may not transfer directly to strongly forced or higher-concentration particle-laden flows.
paper_title: Preferential concentration in a periodically forced particle-laden turbulent planar jet
